entries.reason: Primary self-attributed performer credit, exact original version and complete extent credibly meet human-performance floor. Previous hold imposed an unnecessarily strict recording-method wording requirement; no specific conflicting MIDI evidence remains. This is evidence-based acceptance of a human recording with likely overdubbing, not certification of live quartet or recording method.

findings.finding: IDENTITY: exact audio #843101 explicitly credits Paul Trapkus as Performers, separately from uploader Ptrapkus. Independently established violinist identity plus affirmative primary performer attribution supports human performance; absence of the word multitrack is not contrary evidence. Recordings (1) versus Synthesized/MIDI (0) corroborates but does not alone establish humanity.

VERSION: original four-violin work, not an arrangement; no alternative scoring is attached to the recording. One named performer across four simultaneous violin lines is consistent with human overdubbing, which is accepted; no claim of a live four-person ensemble or independently verified recording method is made.
EXTENT: Complete Recording #843101 lasts 5:00, matching single-movement five-minute whole work. No excerpt indication. All four excluded performers absent from sole primary performer credit.
Complete 14-page score visually inspected through final cadence. Four independent violin staves confirm scoring. Grade-setting long semiquaver passages occur beyond original p.2 sample.

limitations: Audio not independently auditioned; method inferred rather than explicitly documented.

grade.basis: BLIND vote, before reading prior numeric grades: all 14 score pages inspected against data/source/levels.json. Whole-work advanced (ABRSM 8 / RCM 9) estimate. Violin I combines exposed sustained upper-register intonation and quiet entries (pp.1,3,7,11,13) with long repeated slurred semiquaver cells at quarter=140–150 (pp.6–7,9–14), shifts and rapid register changes. Violin II and III inherit semiquaver texture; IV maintains near-continuous quaver string-crossing ostinato and some double stops. Changes among 4/4,6/4,3/4 and staggered sustained entrances need ensemble discipline. Mostly tonal repeated cells and limited chromaticism keep it below routine diploma demands; optional top notes in IV do not set grade.
